children.translated_text: He who knows separately the twenty operations beginning with addition,

children.text: %aṣṭau ca vyavahārān chāyā-antān bhavati gaṇakas sas//
children.translated_text: and the eight procedures ending with shadow [calculations] — he is a mathematician.
The numerators and denominators of two quantities, multiplied by the reciprocal denominators, become equal-denominated;

children.text: saṅkalite aṃśās yojyās vyavakalite aṃśa-antaram kāryam//
children.translated_text: in addition, the numerators are to be joined; in subtraction, the difference of the numerators is to be taken.
Integers, multiplied by the denominator and added to the numerator, [convert them] for two or many [fractions];
the product [of fractions] is the product of the numerators divided by the product of the denominators.
Having inverted the numerator and denominator of the divisor, the denominator multiplied by the denominator,
the numerator multiplied by the numerator — this is the division of reduced [fractions].
The square of the reduced numerator divided by the square of the denominator is the square [of the fraction];
the square root of the reduced numerator divided by the square root of the denominator is the [square] root.
Place the cube of the last [digit]; the square of the last, multiplied by three times the next, [is subtracted] from the first;

children.text: uttara-kṛtis antya-guṇā %tri-guṇā ca uttara-ghanas ca ghanas//
children.translated_text: the square of the next multiplied by the last, tripled, and the cube of the next — [this gives] the cube.
The denominator from the second [group]; the square of the cube root, tripled — the square of the quotient
is to be subtracted, tripled and multiplied by the previous, from the first [group]; from cubing, [one obtains] the cube root.
The sum of the numerators with equal denominators, divided by the denominator, is the result in the first class [of fractions];
in the second class, numerators are multiplied by numerators, and denominators by denominators.
In the third class, for two [fractions] of the first and last, the upper numerators [are] multiplied by the denominators;
the denominators multiplied by the denominators — the upper numerators increased or decreased by their own numerators.

children.text: trairāśike pramāṇam phalam iccā ādi-antayos sadṛśa-rāśī/
children.translated_text: In the rule of three (<s>trairāśika</s>), the measure, the fruit, and the desire — the similar quantities [placed] at the beginning and end;

children.text: icchā phalena guṇitā pramāṇa-bhaktā phalam bhavati//
children.translated_text: the desire multiplied by the fruit and divided by the measure is the result.
The result of the inverse rule of three is the product of the measure and the fruit divided by the desire;
in the [compound] rules of three and so forth, the result [is obtained] in odd [sets] up to eleven.
The transposition of the result: on both sides, the product of the many [quantities] divided by the product of the few — this is to be known;
thus for integers; for fractions, on both sides, the transposition of the denominators.
First, the exchange of prices in barter; the rest is as stated [above].
The operations for the eight procedures have been stated.
The principal multiplied by the time and divided by the fruit, diminished by one, multiplied by the rate — [this gives] the time;
divided by the fruit plus one — the sum of principal and interest becomes the principal.
The product of time and principal, divided by the other time — twice; from the product of the first mixture,
added to the square of half the other, the square root, diminished by half the other — [gives] the principal and interest.
The gains [are found] by multiplying the contributions by the quotient obtained by dividing the total profit by the sum of contributions;
with diminished or increased increments, [multiply] by that [quotient] increased or decreased; [each one's] share is decreased or increased.
The number of terms minus one, multiplied by the common difference, added to the first term — [this is] the last term;
half the sum of the first and last terms is the middle term; multiplied by the number of terms — [this is] the sum.
The square of the remainder of twice the first term minus the common difference, added to eight times the product of the sum and the common difference —
the square root of this, diminished by the remainder, divided by twice the common difference — [gives] the number of terms.
If [the series has] common difference one and first term one, the sum of the desired number of terms
multiplied by the number of terms plus two, divided by three — [this is] the sum of sums (<s>saṅkalita-saṅkalita</s>).
That [number of terms], multiplied by twice the number of terms plus one, divided by three — this is the sum of squares;
the sum of cubes is the square of that [sum]; the piles of these are [made] with equal spheres.
The approximate area [of a quadrilateral] is the product of the halves of the sums of opposite sides;
the exact [area] is the square root of the product of the four [quantities each being] half the sum of sides minus [one] side.
The base increased or decreased by the difference of the squares of the sides divided by the base, halved — [gives] the two segments (<s>āvādha</s>);
the square root of the square of a side minus the square of its own segment is the perpendicular (<s>avalamba</s>).
The square root of the sum of the products of the two pairs of adjacent sides of a non-equilateral quadrilateral is the diagonal;
the square root of the square of the diagonal minus the square of half the sum of the top and base is the perpendicular.

children.text: karṇa-kṛtes koṭi-kṛtim viśodhya mūlam bhujas bhujasya kṛtim/
children.translated_text: Subtracting the square of the upright from the square of the hypotenuse, the square root is the base; subtracting the square of the base,
the root is the upright; the square root of the sum of the squares of the upright and the base is the hypotenuse.
The upper and lower segments [are found from] the sum of the diagonals, or [from] the sum of the diagonal and perpendicular;
the two segments, divided by their own sum — the two products of diagonal and perpendicular [give the segments] separately.
The diagonal multiplied by the lateral side of a non-equilateral [quadrilateral], divided by twice the perpendicular —
[gives] the heart[-line]; for a scalene [triangle], half the square root of the sum of the squares of a side and its opposite.
For a triangle, the product of the two sides divided by twice the perpendicular is the heart-cord (<s>hṛdaya-rajju</s>);
that doubled — the diameter of the circle touching the vertices of a triangle or quadrilateral.
The sum of the products of the sides adjacent to each diagonal, [taken] both ways, divided by each other, multiplied
by the product of opposite sides — the square roots are the two diagonals of a scalene [quadrilateral].
In a scalene quadrilateral, having separately conceived two scalene triangles in the middle,

children.text: karṇa-%dvayena pūrva-vat āvādhe lambakau ca pṛthak//
children.translated_text: the two segments and two perpendiculars [are found] separately by the two diagonals as before.
In the inner triangle of a scalene [quadrilateral], having conceived the two diagonals as two sides, their segments
[are found] separately; the upper and lower segments [are obtained by] the sum of the diagonals, the lower of the diagonals.

children.text: %tri-bhje bhujau tu bhūmis tad-lambas lambaka-adharam khaṇḍam/
children.translated_text: In the triangle, the two sides are the base; its perpendicular is the lower segment of the perpendicular;
the upper segment of the perpendicular is half the sum of the perpendiculars minus the lower.
The segments [are found from] the sum of the diagonal and perpendicular; the lower of the diagonal and perpendicular,
by proportion; in the decreased upper [segment], for a needle[-shaped figure] and a slab.
The sum of the squares of two unequal quantities is the hypotenuse; twice their product is the upright;
twice the difference of the squares of the unequal [quantities] is the base of an isosceles triangle.
The square of a chosen [number] divided by two chosen [numbers] in two ways — the results increased and decreased by the chosen [number], halved —
[give] the two sides of a scalene triangle; the base is the sum of the result decreased by the chosen [number] halved.

children.text: iṣṭasya bhujasya kṛtis bhaktā ūnā iṣṭena tad-#dalam koṭis/
children.translated_text: The square of a chosen side, divided [by another chosen number] and diminished by it, halved — [gives] the upright;
increased by the chosen [number gives] the hypotenuse of a rectangle.

children.text: āyata-karṇas bāhū bhuja-kṛtis iṣṭena bhājitā iṣṭa-ūnā/
children.translated_text: The hypotenuse of a rectangle [and] its sides: the square of one side divided by the chosen [number], diminished by the chosen,
halved, increased [gives] the upright; the base is [the result] increased; for an isosceles trapezium, the face is decreased.
Three of the sides equal to the square of the hypotenuse; the fourth, subtracting the square of the upright

children.text: bāhu-kṛtes %tri-guṇāyās yadi adhikas bhūs mukham hīnas//
children.translated_text: from three times the square of the side — if greater, [it is] the base; the face is less.
The uprights and bases of two right triangles, multiplied by each other's hypotenuses, [are] the sides of a scalene quadrilateral;

children.text: adhikas bhūs mukha-hīnas bāhu-%dvitayam bhujau anyau//
children.translated_text: the base is the greater; the face is the lesser; the other two sides are the remaining pair.
The height of the hill multiplied by the chosen multiplier [and] the distance between the cities, unchanged,
divided by the multiplier plus two — [gives] the leap of one, [assuming] equal speeds.
The diameter and the square of the half-diameter [give] the practical circumference and area when multiplied by three;
from their squares multiplied by ten, the [respective] square roots are the exact [values].
In a circle, the square root of the diameter diminished by the arrow and multiplied by four times the arrow is the chord;
the square of the chord divided by four times the arrow, plus the arrow, is the diameter.
From the difference of the squares of the chord and diameter, the square root — half the difference from the diameter — is the smaller arrow;
the two diameters multiplied by [the diameter] minus the overlap, divided by the sum minus the overlap — [give] the two arrows.
The squares of the half-chords, divided by the two arrows, added to the arrows — [give] the two diameters;

children.text: śarayos phalayos aikyam grāsas grāsa-ūnam aikyam tat//
children.translated_text: the sum of the arrows is the overlap; the sum minus the overlap is that [total diameter].
The area multiplied by the depth is the volume of a uniform excavation; divided by three [gives] that of a needle[-shaped pit];
the sums of the corresponding sides of the top and base, each divided by their count, [are] the mean cords.
The area of [the figure with sides equal to] half the sum of the top and base, multiplied by the depth, is the practical volume;
half the sum of the areas of the top and base, multiplied by the depth, is the <s>autra</s> (second) volume.
Subtracting the practical volume from the <s>autra</s> volume, dividing the remainder by three,

children.text: labdham vyavahāra-phale prakṣipya bhavati phalam sūkṣmam//
children.translated_text: and adding the quotient to the practical volume gives the exact volume.
The area of the shape multiplied by the height; half the sum of the top and base [areas] multiplied by the height and length
is the solid volume; divided by the solid volume of a [single] brick gives the number of bricks.
The product of breadth, length, and thickness in <s>aṅgulas</s>, multiplied by the number of cuts, divided by twice four —
the quotient in <s>kiṣku</s>-<s>aṅgulas</s>; that multiplied by ninety-six is the work [measure].
For <s>śākā</s>-wood and the like, for <s>śālmali</s> (silk-cotton) [the measure] is two hundred; for <s>bījaka</s>, one hundred and twenty;
for <s>śāla</s>, <s>sarala</s> (pine), and the like, one hundred; and for sheep-wood (<s>avi-dāru</s>), sixty-four.
The ninth [measure applies] for grain with husks; the tenth for coarse [grains]; the eleventh applies for fine [grains].
The depth of the circumference — the circumference, multiplied by the square of one-sixth [of itself], is the volume.
The circumference, multiplied by two-fourths or one-third, [applies] at a wall, inside, outside, or at a corner;
computing the area as before, that volume divided by the square of its own multiplier [gives the adjusted result].
Half the day divided by the shadow plus the person [height] plus one [gives] the elapsed and remaining [time] for the east and west;
half the day divided by the fraction of the elapsed or remaining [time of] the day [gives] the shadow minus the person plus one.
The distance between the base of the lamp and the base of the gnomon, multiplied by the desired measure of the gnomon,
subtracting the gnomon from the height of the lamp-flame, divided by the remainder — [this gives] the shadow.
The shadow multiplied by the distance between the tips of the shadows, divided by the difference of the shadows — [gives] the ground [distance];
the ground [distance] multiplied by the gnomon, divided by the shadow — [gives] the height of the lamp-flame.
The multiplicand, [placed in rows] equal to the parts of the multiplier, arranged in the <s>gomūtrikā</s> (zigzag) pattern, multiplied,
and added together — [this gives] the product; or [the multiplicand is made] equal to the divisions of the multiplier.
The multiplicand quantity, [multiplied] by the multiplier quantity increased or decreased by a chosen [number],
decreased or increased by the product of the multiplicand and the chosen [number] — [this] is to be done when the multiplier is greater or less.

children.text: chedena iṣṭa-yuta-ūnena āptam bhājyāt anaṣṭam iṣṭa-guṇam/
children.translated_text: The dividend divided by the divisor increased or decreased by a chosen [number] gives an unchanged [quotient] multiplied by the chosen;
divided by the original divisor, the quotient increased or decreased — [gives] the unchanged [result].
The multiplicand is the product of the divisor and the quotient; divided by the multiplicand [gives] the multiplier;
divided by the divisor [gives] the quotient; the product of the multiplicand and multiplier divided by the quotient [gives] the divisor.
If, of the multiplicand and multiplier [and] of the divisor and quotient, two [pairs of] two are destroyed,

children.text: teṣām dṛśyau vyastau kṛtvā tad-sthānayos ca iṣṭau//
children.translated_text: then, making their visible [forms] interchanged and placing chosen [values] in those positions [one can recover them].

children.text: guṇyam guṇa-kāram vā guṇayet chedena bhāga-hārasya/
children.translated_text: One should multiply the multiplicand or the multiplier by the denominator of the divisor;
of the multiplicand and multiplier quantities, [one] multiplied by the denominator is the divisor.

children.text: acchedasya chedam #rūpam kṛtvā anyat ukta-vat sarvam/
children.translated_text: For [a number] without a denominator, making unity the denominator, everything else is as stated;

children.text: apavartyau cheda-guṇau tulyena iṣṭena guṇyau vā//
children.translated_text: the denominator and multiplier, reduced by the same chosen [common factor], or the multiplicands [may be simplified].
A whole [number] multiplied by sixty parts of its own seconds, divided by thirty — the square of the seconds
is to be added to the square of the whole; squares and cubes are products of two and three equal [factors].
Twice the quantity diminished [by a chosen number], multiplied [by it] many times, added to the square of the diminished — [gives] the square;

children.text: rāśes iṣṭa-yuta-ūnāt vadhas kṛtis vā iṣṭa-kṛti-yuktas//
children.translated_text: or the product of the quantity increased and decreased by a chosen [number], plus the square of the chosen — [gives] the square.
The squares of the chosen [number] and the lesser quantity, increased or decreased by the squares of the other's seconds,
divided by twice the other quantity, by that increased or decreased [give the roots].
The quotient obtained at intermediate positions, by which it is equal to the result-plus-or-minus denominator
halved — the square root of the difference of the sum of squares — or the other, plus or minus the result.

children.text: dik-mātram etat anyat jyā-utpattau kuṭṭake ca kathayiṣye/
children.translated_text: This is only an indication; the rest I shall state in the [chapters on] sine-generation and <s>kuṭṭaka</s> [equations].
In [the topics beginning with] addition, [there are] sixty-six <s>āryā</s> [verses]; the twelfth chapter.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter in the illustrious <s>Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta</s>. //12//

children.text: prāyeṇa yatas praśnās kuṭṭākārāt ṛte na śakyante/
children.translated_text: Since most problems cannot, without the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> [method],

children.text: jñātum vakṣyāmi tatas kuṭṭākāram saha praśnais//
children.translated_text: be solved, I shall therefore state the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> together with the problems.
By [mastery of] <s>kuṭṭaka</s>, zero, negative and positive [numbers], unknowns, elimination of the middle [term], single-color [equations], and products [of unknowns],
the teacher becomes [recognized as] a knower of mathematical sciences (<s>tantra</s>); and also by [mastery of] the square-nature [equation] (<s>varga-prakṛti</s>).
From the divisor of the greater remainder, the divisor of the lesser remainder — the residue

children.text: yat tat paraspara-hṛtam labdham adhas adhas pṛthak sthāpyam//
children.translated_text: of their mutual division — the quotients are to be placed separately one below the other.

children.text: śeṣam tathā iṣṭa-guṇitam yathā agrayos antareṇa saṃyuktam/
children.translated_text: The remainder, multiplied by a chosen [number] such that, when combined with the difference of the two remainders,

children.text: śudhyati guṇakas sthāpyas labdham ca antyāt upāntya-guṇas//
children.translated_text: it is exactly divisible — the multiplier is to be placed, and the quotient, from the last; the penultimate multiplied [by the last].
[Each entry] multiplied by its upper, added to the last — the final [result], divided by the lesser-remainder divisor — the residue,
multiplied by the greater-remainder divisor and added to the greater remainder — becomes the [desired] remainder.
Twice the product of the divisors is the period (<s>yuga</s>); the product of the divisors [is] the elapsed [portion] of the period; the remainder of the two
[is found] by the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> [method]; thus the elapsed [portion] of the period for three or more planets is computed.
The remainder of the revolutions and so forth is the remainders; divided by the divisor [gives] zero; and divided by the day-born remainder,
the remainder of these, divided by the revolution-and-day-born remainder — [gives] the day-count.
The day-born and revolution remainders, by which multiplied [give] the circle and other remainders
divided by the equal divisor — that product is the initial day-count, from this.
When divided mutually, the remainders of the multiplier and divisor —

children.text: tena hṛtau nis-chedau tau eva parasparam hṛtayos//
children.translated_text: divided by that, [they become] without remainder; those very [reduced numbers], mutually divided,

children.text: labdham adhas adhas sthāpyam tathā iṣṭa-guṇa-kāra-saṅguṇam śeṣam/
children.translated_text: the quotients are to be placed one below the other; the remainder, multiplied by the chosen multiplier,

children.text: śudhyati yathā %eka-hīnam guṇakas sthāpyas phalam ca antyāt//
children.translated_text: such that it is divisible by one less — the multiplier is to be placed, and the result from the last.

children.text: agra-antam upāntyena sva-ūrdhvas guṇitas antya-saṃyutas bhaktam/
children.translated_text: The final [value] multiplied by the penultimate, [each] multiplied by its upper, added to the last, divided
by the remainder-free divisor — thus the permanent <s>kuṭṭaka</s>; the remainder [is obtained].
From the desired revolution-remainder, [multiplied] by its own <s>kuṭṭaka</s>-multiplier, [multiplied] by its own divisor,
the remainder is the day-count — added to the elapsed [period] multiplied by the reduced divisor.

children.text: evam sameṣu viṣameṣu ṛṇam dhanam dhanam ṛṇam yat uktam tat/
children.translated_text: Thus for even [numbers of quotients]; for odd, what was stated as negative [becomes] positive and positive [becomes] negative —
the reversal of negative and positive is to be applied to the multiplicand and the addend.

children.text: guṇakas chedas chedas guṇakas dhanam ṛṇam ṛṇam dhanam kāryam/
children.translated_text: The multiplier [becomes] the divisor, the divisor [becomes] the multiplier; positive [becomes] negative, negative [becomes] positive;

children.text: vargam padam padam kṛtis antyāt viparītam ādyam tat//
children.translated_text: the square [becomes] the root, the root [becomes] the square — the inverse from the last is the first.

children.text: yas jānāti yuga-ādi graha-yuga-yātais pṛthak pṛthak kathitais/
children.translated_text: He who knows the elapsed [portion] of the era from the planetary period-elapsed [values] stated separately,
for two, three, four, and more [planets] — he knows the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.

children.text: bha-gaṇa-ādyam iṣṭa-śeṣam kadā indu-divase raves guru-dine vā/
children.translated_text: On which day of the Moon, or day of the Sun, or day of <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), the desired remainder of revolutions and so forth [occurs] —

children.text: jña-dine rāśīn kathayati kuṭṭākāram sas jānāti//
children.translated_text: he who states the zodiacal signs on a day of Mercury (<s>Jña</s>) — he knows the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.

children.text: jña-dine yat aṃśa-śeṣam vikalā-śeṣam kadā tat indu-dine/
children.translated_text: The degree-remainder on a day of Mercury — the seconds-remainder, when [does it occur] on a day of the Moon,

children.text: bhānos atha vā śaśinas yas kathayati kuṭṭaka-jñas sas//
children.translated_text: of the Sun, or of the Moon? — he who states [this] is a knower of the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.

children.text: tithi-māna-dineṣu iṣṭās ye arka-ādyās te punar kadā teṣu/
children.translated_text: On the days of a <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), the desired [positions] of the Sun and so forth — when do they [recur] again on those [days]?
On the days of the desired planet — he who states [this] is a knower of the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.
From the desired revolution-remainder, the day-count is obtained by the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>;

children.text: tad-cheda-dinais tāvat dina-vāras yāvat iṣṭas syāt//
children.translated_text: to that, [add] the divisor-days until the day-of-the-week is as desired.

children.text: yas rāśi-ādīn dṛṣṭvā madhyasya iṣṭasya katahyati dyu-gaṇam/
children.translated_text: He who, having seen the zodiacal signs and so forth, computes the day-count of the desired mean [planet]
from the conjunction of two or more planets, or from the difference between planets — he is a knower of the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.
From the remainder-free divisor, multiplied by the sign-degrees-minutes and so forth, and divided
by the revolution-minutes — the quotient is the circle-remainder; from this, the day-count.
Similarly, from the remainder of signs, degrees, minutes, and seconds — the day-count as before;

children.text: naṣṭa-stheṣu iṣṭān tān kṛtvā bhaktvā ukta-vat śeṣam//
children.translated_text: for lost [planetary positions], having made the desired [values] and dividing as stated, the remainder.
From the stated remainder of signs, degrees, minutes, and seconds — the lost [values]

children.text: yas sādhayati uparitanān sa-madhyamān kuṭṭaka-jñas sas//
children.translated_text: he who derives the upper and middle [values] from the desired — he is a knower of the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.

children.text: yena guṇas śeṣa-yutas chedas śudhyati hṛtas sva-guṇakena/
children.translated_text: The divisor, multiplied by which and added to the remainder, is exactly divisible — divided by its own multiplier,

children.text: tad-bhuktam śeṣam phalam evam śeṣāt graha-dyu-gaṇau//
children.translated_text: that daily motion and the remainder [give] the result; thus from the remainder, [one obtains] the planet and the day-count.

children.text: jānāti yas yuga-gatam kathitāt adhimāsa-śeṣakāt iṣṭāt/
children.translated_text: He who knows the elapsed [portion] of the era from the stated desired intercalary-month remainder,

children.text: avama-avaśeṣatas vā tad-yogāt vā sas kuṭṭa-jñas//
children.translated_text: or from the omitted-day remainder, or from their combination — he is a knower of the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.
On the desired solar days, the intercalary-month or omitted-night remainder —

children.text: bhūyas te yas kathayati pṛthak pṛthak vā sas kuṭṭa-jñas//
children.translated_text: he who states when they [recur] again, separately — he is a knower of the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.
From the degree-remainder diminished by three, divided by seven — the square root, diminished by eight,
multiplied by nine, plus one — when does [it equal] one hundred on a Wednesday for the Sun?
From the intercalary-month remainder diminished by three — the square root, increased by two, divided by six,
diminished by two, squared, increased by nine — when does ninety occur?
The square of the omitted-day remainder, minus one, divided by twenty, plus two,
multiplied by eight, divided by ten, plus two — when does eighteen occur?

children.text: dhanayos dhanam ṛṇam ṛṇayos dhana-ṛṇayos antaram sama-aikyam #kham/
children.translated_text: The sum of two positives is positive; of two negatives, negative; of a positive and negative, [their] difference; of two equals, zero;
the sum of negative and zero is negative, of positive and zero is positive; of two zeros, zero.

children.text: ūnam adhikāt viśodhyam dhanam dhanāt ṛṇam ṛṇāt adhikam ūnāt/
children.translated_text: The lesser is to be subtracted from the greater: positive from positive, negative from negative; the greater from the lesser —

children.text: vyastam tad-antaram syāt ṛṇam dhanam dhanam ṛṇam bhavati//
children.translated_text: that difference becomes reversed: negative [becomes] positive, positive [becomes] negative.
Zero minus negative is negative; [zero minus] positive is positive; [zero minus zero] is zero, space;

children.text: śodhyam yadā dhanam ṛṇāt ṛṇam dhanāt vā tadā kṣepyam//
children.translated_text: when positive is to be subtracted from negative, or negative from positive — then it is to be added.

children.text: ṛṇam ṛṇa-dhanayos ghātas dhanam ṛṇayos dhana-vadhas dhanam bhavati/
children.translated_text: The product of negative and positive is negative; of two negatives, positive; of two positives, positive;
the product of zero and negative, of zero and positive, or of zero and zero — is zero.

children.text: dhana-bhaktam dhanam ṛṇa-hṛtam ṛṇam dhanam bhavati #kham #kha-bhaktam #kham/
children.translated_text: Positive divided by positive is positive; negative divided by negative is positive; zero divided by zero is zero;

children.text: bhaktam ṛṇena dhanam ṛṇam dhanena hṛtam ṛṇam ṛṇam bhavati//
children.translated_text: A positive quantity divided by a negative is negative; a negative divided by a positive is negative; a negative divided by a negative becomes positive.

children.text: #kha-uddhṛtam ṛṇam dhanam vā tad-chedam #kham ṛṇa-dhana-vibhaktam vā/
children.translated_text: Zero divided by a negative or positive quantity is zero; a negative or positive divided by zero remains that quantity with zero as denominator.

children.text: ṛṇa-dhanayos vargas svam #kham #khasya padam kṛtis yat tat//
children.translated_text: The square of a positive or negative is positive; zero squared is zero; the square root of zero is zero; and that which is a perfect square has a root.
The sum increased or decreased by the difference, halved, is the <s>saṅkramaṇa</s> (concurrence); or it is the difference divided by the difference.
The difference of squares, increased or decreased by the difference, halved, is the <s>viṣamakarma</s> (operation for unequal quantities).

children.text: karaṇī lambas tad-kṛtis iṣṭa-hṛtā iṣṭa-ūna-saṃyutā alpā bhūs/
children.translated_text: The <s>karaṇī</s> (surd): the perpendicular is the square of it, divided by an assumed quantity, and diminished or increased by the assumed quantity; the smaller is the base;
the larger, halved, is the hypotenuse. That whose product is a perfect square is to be reduced.
The square of the sum of the square root of the <s>karaṇī</s> divided by an assumed number and the assumed number, multiplied by the assumed number; or the square of their difference.

children.text: guṇyas tiryak adhas adhas guṇaka-samas tad-guṇas sahitas//
children.translated_text: The multiplicand is placed crosswise, below and below; the multiplier is equal to that; its product is added.
The dividend and divisor are multiplied by the desired additive or subtractive quantity's own denominators, separately, repeatedly making them even;
or the dividend is divided by the denominator reduced to unity. A square is the product of two equal quantities.
Of the unity diminished by the desired <s>karaṇī</s>, the halves of the square root increased and decreased by unity:

children.text: %prathamam rūpāṇi anyat tatas dvitīyam karaṇī asakṛt//
children.translated_text: the first is the integer part, the other thereafter is the second, the <s>karaṇī</s>, applied repeatedly.
Of unknown squares, cubes, fourth powers, fifth powers, sixth powers, and so on —
like terms are to be added or subtracted; unlike terms are kept separate.
The product of two equal quantities is the square; the product of three or more equal quantities is the corresponding power; the product of different species
is the mutual product of the unknowns, called <s>bhāvitaka</s> (product of unknowns). The rest proceeds as before.
The difference of the absolute terms divided by the difference of the unknowns, transposed, gives the unknown when the unknowns are equal;
the square unknowns are to be subtracted from whichever side has the absolute terms, and the absolute terms placed below those.
The absolute terms multiplied by four times the coefficient of the square term,

combined with the square of the coefficient of the middle term, the square root of this, diminished by the middle coefficient and divided by twice the square coefficient, is the middle term (the unknown).
The absolute terms multiplied by the square coefficient, combined with the square of half the unknown coefficient — the
square root of this, diminished by half the unknown coefficient, divided by the square coefficient, is the unknown.
From the remainder of the fractional part increased by one, twelve times four, added to eight,
when equal to the remainder of the fractional part increased by one — then state the elapsed days (<s>ahargaṇa</s>).
The intercalary month remainder diminished by two, divided by three, increased by seven, multiplied by two,
when equal to the intercalary month remainder — then state the elapsed portion of the <s>yuga</s> (astronomical cycle).
The omitted day remainder diminished by one, divided by six, increased by three, of the omitted day remainder
divided by five, when equal — then state the elapsed portion of the <s>yuga</s>.
From the revolution remainder diminished by two, the square root, diminished by one, multiplied by ten, increased by two,

children.text: maṇḍala-śeṣam vi-%ekam bhānos jña-dine kadā bhavati//
children.translated_text: when equal to the revolution remainder diminished by one — on which day of the Sun is <s>Budha's</s> (Mercury's) day?
When the square of the intercalary month remainder's quarter diminished by three equals the intercalary month remainder,
or from the omitted day remainder, when does it equal the omitted day remainder?

children.text: ādyāt varṇāt anyān varṇān prohya ādya-mānam āḍya-hṛtam/
children.translated_text: From the first unknown, removing the other unknowns, the value of the first divided by the first's coefficient;
the two with equal denominators, repeatedly, transposed — the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> (pulverizer method) applies when there are many unknowns.
From the elapsed days combined with the past revolutions, combined with their remainder, combined with their sum —

children.text: tad-yogāt dyu-gaṇam vā yas kathayati kuṭṭaka-jñas sas//
children.translated_text: he who can determine the elapsed days from their total is one who knows the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.
From the elapsed days diminished by past revolutions, diminished by their remainder, diminished by their sum,

children.text: tad-vivarāt dyu-gaṇam vā yas kathayati kuṭṭaka-jñas sas//
children.translated_text: or from their difference — he who can determine the elapsed days is one who knows the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.
By the remainders of signs and so on, and similarly, diminished by the elapsed intercalary months and days,

children.text: tad-śeṣais ca yuga-gatam yas kathayati kuṭṭaka-jñas sas//
children.translated_text: and from their remainders — he who can determine the elapsed portion of the <s>yuga</s> is one who knows the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.

children.text: aṃśaka-śeṣeṇa yutāt liptā-śeṣāt tad-antarāt atha vā/
children.translated_text: From the remainder of the degrees combined with, or from the remainder of the minutes, or from their difference —

children.text: bhānos jña-dine dyu-gaṇam yas kathayati kuṭṭaka-jñas sas//
children.translated_text: he who can determine the elapsed days on <s>Budha's</s> (Mercury's) day from the Sun is one who knows the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.
When is the degree remainder equal to three, the minute remainder on <s>Budha's</s> day of the Sun
equal to six, seven, eight, or nine — the calculator determines this within a year.
Making the degree remainder equal to the degree remainder, or the minute remainder equal to the minute remainder,

children.text: divasa-karasya iṣṭa-dine kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: of the Sun on a desired day — the calculator determines this within a year.
The omitted day remainder equal to the omitted days, the intercalary month remainder equal to the intercalary months,

children.text: iṣṭa-yuta-ūnam tulyam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: increased or decreased by a desired amount and made equal — the calculator determines this within a year.
The Sun's fractional parts without remainder: seventy times the Sun, diminished by the degree remainder,
is purified when divided by ten thousand — the calculator determines this within a year.
In a <s>bhāvitaka</s>: the product of the absolute terms with the unknowns, the product involving unknowns, divided by an assumed quantity — the two assumed results;

children.text: alpe adhikas adhike alpas kṣepyas bhāvita-hṛtau vyastam//
children.translated_text: to the lesser is added the excess from the greater; the quotient from the <s>bhāvitaka</s> divisor is transposed.
From the product of the Sun's sign and degree portions, subtracting the sign-degrees multiplied by three and four,

children.text: %navatim dṛṣṭvā sūryam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: seeing ninety and the Sun — the calculator determines this within a year.
In a <s>bhāvitaka</s>, the quantities whose product with the lost unknown equals those amounts,
are assumed as desired; the sum of the unknowns multiplied by those becomes the absolute terms.
The product of the measures of the unknowns with the <s>bhāvitaka</s> gives the count of the desired unknown — thus

children.text: sidhyati vinā api bhāvita-sama-karaṇāt kim kṛtam tat atas//
children.translated_text: it is solved even without the <s>bhāvitaka</s> equation; what then is accomplished by it?

children.text: mūlam dvidhā iṣṭa-vargāt guṇaka-guṇāt iṣṭa-yuta-vihīnāt ca/
children.translated_text: The root is twofold: from the product of the assumed square and the multiplier, increased and decreased by the assumed quantity,

children.text: ādya-vadhas guṇaka-guṇas saha antya-ghātena kṛtam antyam//
children.translated_text: the product of the first pair multiplied by the multiplier, together with the product of the last pair, gives the last.
The sum of the cross-products is the first; the additive equals the product of the additives.
When the roots are divided by the additive or subtractive, the additive becomes unity.
From the roots when the additive is unity, separately, with the roots of the desired additive or subtractive,

children.text: kṛtvā antya-ādya-pade ye prakṣepe śodhane vā iṣṭe//
children.translated_text: forming the last and first roots — for any desired additive or subtractive.
The square of the last root increased by four, diminished by three, halved, multiplied by the last root, gives the last root;
the square of the last root diminished by one, halved, multiplied by the first root, gives the first root.
When the square of the last root is diminished by four, or increased by three and one, the half of the product, separately, diminished by one;
this multiplied by the first root gives the last; the product of the roots multiplied by the multiplier gives the first; that is the last root.

children.text: varge guṇake kṣepas kena cit uddhṛta-yuta-ūnitas dalitas/
children.translated_text: When the additive in the square-multiplier is divided by some quantity, increased or diminished and halved,
the first is the last root; the other, divided by the square root of the multiplier coefficient, is the first.
When the multiplier is divisible by a perfect square, the first is divided by its square root;
when the additive is divisible by a perfect square, the roots are multiplied by its square root.
The sum of the multipliers multiplied by eight, divided by the square of the difference of the multipliers, gives a quantity;
the two multipliers tripled, transposed with the excess, divided by the difference, give the roots.
A square increased or decreased by another square, divided by the square of half the sum or difference of those,
multiplied by them, added and subtracted, gives two squares; and in the product, unity is added.

children.text: yais ūnas yais ca yutas rūpais vargas tad-aikyam iṣṭa-hṛtam/
children.translated_text: The sum of the unities by which a square is decreased or increased, divided by a desired number,

children.text: iṣṭa-ūnam tad-#dala-kṛtis ūnā abhyadhikā bhavati rāśis//
children.translated_text: that desired number diminished by it — the square of the half, diminished or increased, becomes the quantity.

children.text: yābhyām kṛtis adhika-ūnas tad-antaram hṛta-yuta-ūnam iṣṭena/
children.translated_text: By whichever quantities a square is increased or decreased, their difference, divided and increased or decreased by the desired number,
the square of the half, increased or decreased — gives the quantity for the greater or lesser.
The square of the remainder of the Sun's sign-minutes, multiplied by ninety-two, or multiplied by eighty-three,

children.text: sa-%ekā jña-dine vargam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: increased by one, made a perfect square on <s>Budha's</s> (Mercury's) day — the calculator determines this within a year.
The remainder of the Sun's seconds, multiplied by five decreased, and likewise by ten,

children.text: varge bṛhaspati-dine kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: made a perfect square on <s>Bṛhaspati's</s> (Jupiter's) day — the calculator determines this within a year.
The square of the revolution remainder etc., multiplied by three, increased by nine hundred,

children.text: kṛtim %aṣṭa-%śata-ūnam vā kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: or the square diminished by eight hundred — the calculator determines this within a year.
The square of the revolution remainder etc., multiplied by four, increased by sixty-five,

children.text: %ṣaṣṭi-ūnam vā vargam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: or diminished by sixty, made a perfect square — the calculator determines this within a year.
The desired revolution remainder etc., multiplied by ninety-two decreased, multiplied by eighty-three,

children.text: #rūpeṇa yutam vargam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: increased by unity, made a perfect square — the calculator determines this within a year.
The square of the intercalary month remainder, multiplied by thirteen, increased by three hundred,

children.text: %tri-ghana-ūnam vā vargam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: or diminished by twenty-seven, made a perfect square — the calculator determines this within a year.
The remainder of the Moon's seconds, multiplied by seventeen, and also multiplied by thirteen,

children.text: pṛthak %eka-yutam vargam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: each increased by one, made a perfect square — the calculator determines this within a year.
The square of the omitted day remainder, multiplied by twelve, increased by a hundred,

children.text: %tribhis ūnam vā vargam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: or diminished by three, made a perfect square — the calculator determines this within a year.
On <s>Budha's</s> (Mercury's) day, the Sun's minute remainder, increased or decreased by <s>Bṛhaspati's</s> (Jupiter's) day second remainder,

children.text: vargam vadham ca sa-%ekam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: made a perfect square and a product increased by one — the calculator determines this within a year.
The second remainder, combined with ninety-three and diminished by sixty-seven,

children.text: bhānos jña-dine vargam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: made a perfect square of the Sun on <s>Budha's</s> (Mercury's) day — the calculator determines this within a year.
On <s>Budha's</s> (Mercury's) day, the Sun's minute remainder, increased by twelve and by sixty-three,

children.text: %ṣaṣṭyā %aṣṭabhis ca ūnam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: and diminished by sixty and by eight — the calculator determines this within a year.
From the remainder of the Moon's sub-seconds, the remainder of the Sun's seconds, or the remainder of degrees —

children.text: atha vā madhyamam iṣṭam kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: or else, computing a desired mean [longitude], the calculator [can proceed] for up to a year.
From the remainder of Jupiter's sub-seconds [one finds] the Earth-born [Mercury]; from the remainder of Mars's seconds, the Moon;

children.text: ravim indu-bhāga-śeṣāt kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: from the remainder of the Moon's degrees [one finds] the Sun — the calculator [works thus] for up to a year.
From the desired remainder of a desired planet, the day-count [is found] by multiplying with the elapsed civil [days] reduced by their common divisor,

children.text: cheda-dinais adhikas asmāt anya-graha-śeṣam iṣṭas vā//
children.translated_text: increased by the divisor-days — from this, the remainder of another planet, or a desired [quantity].
The civil-day-divisor and the degree-divisor of two planets, [taken] in reverse order from each other, [are applied] from the day-count
of the two planets — that from which, divided by the respective civil-day-divisor, [the result] is multiplied by the obtained [quotient].
The civil-day-divisor and the degree-divisor, reversed — from their sum, and again from that,
the remainder from the day-count — thus for three and more [planets], as before, on a desired day.

children.text: dyu-gaṇam avama-avaśeṣāt ravi-candrau madhyamau sphuṭau atha vā/
children.translated_text: The day-count from the remainder of the omitted [lunar days] — the mean [longitudes of] the Sun and Moon, whether mean or true;

children.text: evam tithim graham vā kurvan ā vatsarāt gaṇakas//
children.translated_text: thus computing a <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) or a planet, the calculator [works] for up to a year.
The omitted-day remainder multiplied by a single day, diminished by one revolution of the Sun-Moon [difference],

children.text: śudhyati bhū-dina-bhaktam vi-%ekam cāndrais tad-uktis iyam//
children.translated_text: when divided by the terrestrial days, [gives] one less than the lunar [days] — this is the statement thereof.
From the omitted-day remainder multiplied by 108,455 and divided
by 3,506,481 — the day-count and the remainder.
From [the omitted-day remainder] multiplied by 3,249,624, divided by 3,506,481 —
the desired omitted-day remainder — that remainder is the remainder of the Sun's revolutions.
Multiplied by 110,179, divided by 3,562,220 —
the remainder from the omitted-day remainder is the <s>tithis</s>; from the omitted-day remainder, the sub-seconds.

children.text: bhāga-kalā-vikalā-aikyam dṛṣṭvā vikalā-antaram ca ke śeṣe/
children.translated_text: Having observed the sum of degrees, minutes, and sub-seconds, and also the difference of sub-seconds — [these are] the remainders.
The sum divided in two, increased and decreased by the difference — halved [gives] the [two] remainders.
The difference of their squares in the first [case]; that difference, increased and decreased by the difference divided [by it],
the difference of squares divided by two — [gives] the remainder; from that, the day-count.
[From the sum of the products, doubled — subtracting the square of the sum, the root of the remainder;

children.text: tena yuta-ūnas yogas dalitas śeṣe pṛthak abhīṣṭe// Cb.99]
children.translated_text: by that, the sum increased and decreased, halved — [gives] the [two] remainders separately as desired. // Cb.99]
From the product of the remainders multiplied by twice the square, to which the square of the difference of remainders is added — the [square] root;
decreased and increased by the difference of remainders, halved — [gives] the [two] remainders separately as desired.

children.text: hṛdi-ghātram amī praśnās praśnān anyān %sahasra-śas kuryāt/
children.translated_text: These problems [test] the heart and body; one may construct thousands of other problems.

children.text: anyais dattān praśnān uktyā evam sādhayet karaṇais//
children.translated_text: Problems given by others may be solved in this very manner, by the [appropriate] procedures.

children.text: jana-saṃsadi daiva-vidām tejas nāśayati bhānus iva bhānām/
children.translated_text: In a public assembly of astrologers, [such problems] destroy the brilliance [of rivals], as the Sun [destroys that] of the stars,
through <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> (pulverizer) problems, even when merely recited — how much more when [posed] by the hundreds!

children.text: prati-sūtram amī praśnās pathitās sa-uddeśakeṣu sūtreṣu/
children.translated_text: These problems, recited sūtra by sūtra, are in the sūtras with examples.
With one hundred and three <s>āryā</s> verses, the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> [chapter] is the eighteenth chapter.
Thus, in the illustrious <s>Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta</s>, the eighteenth chapter on the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> (pulverizer).

body.translated_text: [Knowledge of the gnomon-shadow and related topics]

children.text: dṛṣṭvā dina-%ardha-ghaṭikā yas arka-jñas akṣa-aṃśakān vijānāti/
children.translated_text: He who, having observed the half-day <s>ghaṭikās</s> (time-units), being a knower of the Sun, determines the degrees of terrestrial latitude —
and from the known [planet], determines the unknown by means of the <s>ghaṭikās</s> of the rising-interval — he is a knower of the system.

children.text: asta-antara-ghaṭikābhis yas jñātāt jñeyam ānayati tastmāt/
children.translated_text: He who, by means of the <s>ghaṭikās</s> of the setting-interval, derives the unknown from the known —

children.text: madhya-gatim yuga-bha-gaṇān ānayati tatas sas tantra-jñas//
children.translated_text: and derives the mean motion and the <s>yuga</s>-revolution numbers from that — he is a knower of the system.
He who derives the measures of the shadow, the Sun, and the Moon's disc from the height of the lamp-flame,
and [determines] the shadow in the knowledge of the ground between the gnomon-base [and the lamp] — he is a knower of the system.

children.text: iṣṭa-gṛha-auccya-jñas yas tad-antara-jñas nirīkṣyate tu jale/
children.translated_text: He who, knowing the height of a desired house and the distance to it, [determines what is] seen in water,

children.text: gṛha-bhitti-agram darśayati darpaṇe vā sas tantra-jñas//
children.translated_text: and shows the top of a house-wall in a mirror — he is a knower of the system.
He who knows the height of a lamp from the knowledge of the distance between the second shadow-tip and [the first],

children.text: śaṅku-chāyā-jñas vā bhūmes chāyām sas tantra-jñas//
children.translated_text: or being a knower of the gnomon-shadow, [determines] the shadow of the ground — he is a knower of the system.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā gṛha-tala-antara-jālabhos dṛṣṭvā agram gṛhasya bhūmi-jñas/
children.translated_text: He who, knowing the ground-distance, having seen through a window the top of a house, and being a knower of the ground,

children.text: vetti gṛha-auccyam dṛṣṭvā taila-stham vā sas tantra-jñas//
children.translated_text: determines the height of a house, or having seen [the reflection] in oil — he is a knower of the system.

children.text: vīkṣya gṛha-agram salile prasārya salilam punar sva-bhū-jñāne/
children.translated_text: He who, having seen the top of a house in water, having extended the water [surface], in the knowledge of its own ground,

children.text: ānayati jalāt bhūmim gṛhasya vā auccyam sas tantra-jñas//
children.translated_text: derives from the water the ground-distance or the height of the house — he is a knower of the system.
He who, with known shadow-persons, having determined the opening between the water and the wall,

children.text: kuḍye arka-tejasas yas vetti ārūḍhim sas tantra-jñas//
children.translated_text: determines the height to which the Sun's rays climb on the wall — he is a knower of the system.
The <s>ghaṭikās</s> of half the desired day — the <s>prāṇas</s> (breaths) of the interval from fifteen <s>ghaṭikās</s>;
these are the <s>caraprāṇas</s> (ascensional difference) of that day — from these, determine the latitude as before.
Of the known and the unknown planets, by the <s>nāḍikās</s> of the rising-interval, increased or decreased

children.text: udayais jñātas jñātāt jñeyas prāk-aparayos jñeyas//
children.translated_text: by the risings, the known [planet yields] the unknown from the known; for eastern and western [planets], the unknown [is found].
The known [planet], with half a revolution added, by the <s>nāḍikās</s> of the setting-interval, increased or decreased —
from the known, for eastern and western [planets], the unknown [is found]; when less than half a revolution, the unknown [is found].

children.text: jñātam kṛtvā madhyam bhūyas anya-dine tad-antaram bhuktis/
children.translated_text: Having computed the known as mean [longitude], the difference on another day is the daily motion.
By the rule of three from the daily motion — the derivation of the <s>kalpa</s> revolution-numbers of a planet.
From half the duration [of the eclipse], the reverse [computation yields] the true measure of the shadow in an eclipse;
from the measure-rising of the Sun and Moon, by the fraction of <s>ghaṭikās</s> from the rising of the [zodiacal] sign.
The distance between the lamp-base and the gnomon-base, multiplied by the measure of the desired gnomon,
divided by the remainder after subtracting the gnomon from the lamp-flame's height — [gives] the shadow.

children.text: śaṅku-antareṇa guṇitā chāyā chāyā-antareṇa bhaktā bhūs /
children.translated_text: The shadow multiplied by the gnomon-interval, divided by the shadow-interval — [gives] the ground [distance].
The ground with the shadow added, multiplied by the gnomon — the lamp's height, divided by the shadow.
Having known the gnomon-shadow, by proportion one may determine the heights
of houses, shrines, trees, and mountains — or knowing the height, [one may determine] the shadow.
The ground-distance, multiplied by the eye-height, divided by the sum of eye and house-height;

children.text: phala-bhūs nyaste toye prati-rūpa-agram gṛhasya narāt//
children.translated_text: the result-distance — when water is placed, the reflection of the house-top [is seen] by the person.
Having seen the house-top in the water between the house and the person — the eye-height multiplied
by the house-to-water distance is the height of the house, divided by the person-to-water distance.
By the difference of the first and second person-to-water distances, divided — the recession of water;
multiplied by the eye-height gives the height; from the water, the ground multiplied by the person-to-water distance.
The water-to-wall distance, divided by the shadow-person — the obtained [result] is the height [of the Sun's rays on the wall].
This is the nineteenth chapter, of twenty <s>āryā</s> verses.
A <s>ṛgvarga</s> (letter-group) is a sequence; a collection-combination, in even-uneven [arrangements] and even [ones] —
those obtained as before — groups of four [in the columns]; the rest combined with the last.
The first and last, with and without the addition of one, and their reverses — as long as
in squares and the like of odd-even [numbers], one increases the quarters in direct and reverse order.
By one each, two by two — in those with additional [syllables] and their bases,
the extension (<s>prastāra</s>) from the square and onwards to the desired end, becomes the <s>yava</s>-middle.
The end-zeros give the top of the two-footed [meter]; the count separately below the initial [syllables] of three-footed [meters];
that, subtracted — the one-less, separately — a unit added above at the end.
As long as the quarter-minus-one [syllables] proceed through the letters — then with increments of one,
the product of [numbers] beginning with one added — the total number of meters from the square onwards.
In odd [meters], above the half-quarter plus one; in even [meters], at the half-quarter;
twice the half minus one — the <s>yula</s>-syllables below all of them.
With the middle [syllables] thus diminished by half, the direct-quarter [gives] the reversed-equal-quarter beginning.
In odd ones, the one-less in the middle — having subtracted, one makes the first from the rest.
The placement with the initial [syllables] equal to one-plus-direct-order — the excess subtracted below.

children.text: saṃkhyaikyaṃ tādṛk yādṛk prathamas trirahito naṣṭe//
children.translated_text: The sum of the [row] numbers is such as the first minus three — in the <s>naṣṭa</s> (lost [meter recovery]).

children.text: mādhyaiḥ kṛtaiś ca dalitaiḥ samasaṃkhyāyāṃ kramotkramāt kṣeppam/
children.translated_text: With the middle [syllables] made and halved — in an even number, the addition from direct and reverse order;

children.text: viṣamāyāṃ vyekāyāṃ dalam kramād uttkramāt saikam//
children.translated_text: in an odd number minus one — halving in direct order, with one added in reverse order.
In an even number, by the direct and reverse staircase order — and likewise for the odd [numbers];
in the <s>pacita</s> (cooked) and <s>dṛṣṭa</s> (seen) [procedures], the first [syllable is found]; the remaining syllables at the end.
Of equal-half, equal, and unequal [meters] — the product of the number, half-quarter, and all arrangements;
the product of one's own initial [numbers] with other quarters — the product of one's own and the next, with one added, as before.
The arrangement next after the first — below; the other-equal beginning as before;
the placement — the square of the other — the extension of half-equal and unequal [meters].
In the <s>naṣṭa</s> [recovery] from the end — one's own below-product minus the arrangement-product of half-equal and unequal [meters];
minus one, separately — divided by one's own square, the result for equal-arrangement [meters].
In the <s>uddiṣṭa</s> (indicated [meter]) — divided by the arrangement, the elapsed [gives] the first; when the result has the same form, another;
repeatedly, with the square-fraction added — with one added, for half-equal and unequal [meters].
In the [individual] syllable-groups, the separate count of heavy and light syllables, divided by [numbers] beginning with one, as before;
in odd [meters], with the initial [syllable] light — with the light [syllables], the <s>Meru</s> [triangular array] for equal [meters] and the like.
After one and two, the next is twice [the preceding]; from the adjacent [number], a two-form [entry] below.
The flag [pattern] (<s>dhvaja</s>) [is obtained] from the halves of the even and odd [numbers] of the square-series and so on, with short [syllables].

children.text: laghusaṃkhyā padadalitā parato'dho'dhaś ca śudhyati hṛtā yaiḥ/
children.translated_text: The count of short [syllables], divided by half the number of feet and then successively below, is purified when divided by those [numbers];
with the purified [values] doubled at the end, placed after the square [values], the mountain [pattern] (<s>mandara</s>) [is obtained] with short [syllables].
Placing below successively, one should set down [numbers] beginning with one and increasing by one; below those,

children.text: svāt parato'nyaikyam adhaḥ prastārād uktavad ihādyaiḥ//
children.translated_text: the sum of the one beyond its own [position] and the one below — from the expansion (<s>prastāra</s>), as stated, with the initial [values].
Sixty guru-[syllable units], each equal to one <s>ghaṭī</s>, doubled, are in single <s>aṅgulas</s> — this would be the count;
twenty-two is [the number] of <s>āryā</s> [verses]. The chapter on prosody and combinatorics (<s>chandaściti</s>) follows.
Thus in the illustrious <s>Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta</s>, the twentieth chapter on prosody and combinatorics.
Having placed digits at the junctions of the feet in the eighth-parts of the signs, in direct and reverse order,
one should construct the chords (<s>jyās</s>) for pairs; their halves [are the half-chords (<s>jyārdhāni</s>)].
The half-chords of the half-chords [are] the sine-differences (<s>jyā-khaṇḍāni</s>), [which are] the intervals.

children.text: vyastāni antyāt atha vā iṣus utkrama-jyā dhanus tābhyām//
children.translated_text: Reversed from the last, or else the versine (<s>iṣu</s>) is the reverse-sine (<s>utkramajyā</s>); the arc (<s>dhanus</s>) [is derived] from these two.
From the square of the semi-diameter (<s>vyāsārdha</s>) multiplied by one, two, and three respectively, [taking] the fourth parts separately,
the square roots are the eight-, twelve-, and sixteen-part divisions; from these, the others [are derived].
One-fourth of the sum of the squares of equal direct-sine and reverse-sine equal-divisions,
subtracted from the square of the semi-diameter, [with] that undestroyed — the square root of that is the first [sine value].
The divisions of half of that, those being less by that [amount], equal to twenty-four — this is the second [method] in the derivation.
[The values are:] four, two, one, ten, eleven, five, seven, six, nine, nine, and so forth.

children.text: evam jīvā-khaṇḍāni alpāni bahūni vā ādya-khaṇḍāni/
children.translated_text: Thus the sine-differences — whether few or many — the initial divisions
are the half-chords of the sixth, fourth, and third parts of the circumference of the circle.
From the diameter multiplied by the equal-division reverse-sine, or else from the fourth part, that which

children.text: kṛtvā ukta-khaṇḍakāni jyā-%ardha-ānayanam na laghu asmāt//
children.translated_text: is obtained by making the stated divisions — the derivation of half-chords is not simpler than this.
